items.title: Bring a tent, I've got the coffee: Lessons from it-sa
items.summary: Thorsten may have had to camp out in Nuremberg to attend it-sa, but the real story is the initiative to add a formal IT Security apprenticeship program in Germany for the thousands of young hackers ready to join our side.

items.title: Appraisal by AI: Model-driven victim prioritization in the VOLTA infostealer
items.summary: The self-deleting VOLTA infostealer steals credentials, sessions, and cryptocurrency wallets. Then, it uses LLMs to profile victims and rank their most valuable assets.

items.title: A quiet week in infosec <.<
items.summary: In this edition of the Threat Source newsletter, William explores how PHP has taken over the conversation, Node.js has joined in, but underneath it all, there are still good people doing good work.

items.title: IR trends Q3 2026: Actors impersonate IT help desks in vishing attacks as ransomware activity increases
items.summary: Phishing remained the leading initial access technique, while percentage of ransomware and pre-ransomware cases increased. Finance and public administration tied as the top-targeted industries.

items.title: NIK C2: The new AI-enabled command-and-control framework
items.summary: Cisco Talos observed a new AI-integrated command-and-control (C2) framework in the wild called “NIK C2.”

items.title: Inside KeyDrift: Analyzing historical UAT-11473 activity on Cisco SD-WAN
items.summary: Talos has identified UAT-11473, a highly sophisticated APT, who exploited CVE-2026-20127, an authentication bypass vulnerability in Cisco SD-WAN Catalyst Controller instances to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to affected systems to deploy KeyDrift.

items.title: From federal SOCs to Talos: Ryan Fetterman on practical security research
items.summary: What does it mean to be "blue collar" for the blue team? Ryan Fetterman discusses the realities of detection engineering, and shares his philosophy on building a career in security without burning out.

items.title: I had plans for that second
items.summary: The Earth is speeding up, the leap second is being abolished, oh, and there's critical vulnerabilities in PHP.

items.title: Compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates
items.summary: Cisco Talos is aware of eight intermediate certificates belonging to the intermediate certificate authority, eMudhra.

items.title: Two critical RCEs in PHP core
items.summary: Two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in PHP core could have implications across its wider ecosystem. Talos has published a blog to explain what we know so far, and details the Snort coverage available, including rules in the Community Ruleset.

items.title: Parasitizing trust: How legitimate infrastructure becomes a delivery pipeline for attackers
items.summary: Adversaries are turning the tools businesses trust into delivery mechanisms for malicious activity. Cisco Talos observed abuse of more than 25 legitimate platforms over the past year, exploiting the built-in trust of collaboration, file-sharing, payment and other services to reach their targets.

items.title: There's only so much code: the rise in vulnerability numbers
items.summary: The September Microsoft Patch Tuesday release included 975 vulnerability advisories. This month, 1,415 vulnerabilities were just dropped. Compared to a pre-June average of 100 a month, that increase is staggering. Where did they come from? And what does the future look like?

items.title: The Q3 Vulnerability Pulse: Discovery ≠ Exploitation
items.summary: Is the cybersecurity world really facing a "Bugmageddon?" Thor breaks down the latest CVE and KEV trends in the latest Threat Source newsletter.

items.title: Break the silence: Kazakhstan-nexus UAT-6275 targets CIS government organizations
items.summary: Talos and Recorded Future identified UAT-6275 activity targeting government organizations across the Commonwealth of Independent States. Recovered artifacts show additional interest in water resources and energy.

items.title: Microsoft Patch Tuesday for October 2026 — Snort rules and prominent vulnerabilities
items.summary: Microsoft has released its monthly security update for October 2026, which includes 1415 vulnerabilities affecting a range of products, including 85 that Microsoft marked as "critical."
